legend: Recently Lynyrd and Skynyrd went to a shop where Lynyrd bought a permutation p%%ZSMJ0%% of length n%%ZSMJ1%%, and Skynyrd bought an array a%%ZSMJ2%% of length m%%ZSMJ3%%, consisting of integers from 1%%ZSMJ4%% to n%%ZSMJ5%%.

Lynyrd and Skynyrd became bored, so they asked you q%%ZSMJ6%% queries, each of which has the following form: "does the subsegment of a%%ZSMJ7%% from the l%%ZSMJ8%%-th to the r%%ZSMJ9%%-th positions, inclusive, have a subsequence that is a cyclic shift of p%%ZSMJ10%%?" Please answer the queries.
A permutation of length n%%ZSMJ11%% is a sequence of n%%ZSMJ12%% integers such that each integer from 1%%ZSMJ13%% to n%%ZSMJ14%% appears exactly once in it.

A cyclic shift of a permutation (p1,p2,…,pn)%%ZSMJ15%% is a permutation (pi,pi+1,…,pn,p1,p2,…,pi−1)%%ZSMJ16%% for some i%%ZSMJ17%% from 1%%ZSMJ18%% to n%%ZSMJ19%%. For example, a permutation (2,1,3)%%ZSMJ20%% has three distinct cyclic shifts: (2,1,3)%%ZSMJ21%%, (1,3,2)%%ZSMJ22%%, (3,2,1)%%ZSMJ23%%.

A subsequence of a subsegment of array a%%ZSMJ24%% from the l%%ZSMJ25%%-th to the r%%ZSMJ26%%-th positions, inclusive, is a sequence ai1,ai2,…,aik%%ZSMJ27%% for some i1,i2,…,ik%%ZSMJ28%% such that l≤i1<i2<…<ik≤r%%ZSMJ29%%.
input: The first line contains three integers n%%ZSMJ30%%, m%%ZSMJ31%%, q%%ZSMJ32%% (1≤n,m,q≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ33%%) — the length of the permutation p%%ZSMJ34%%, the length of the array a%%ZSMJ35%% and the number of queries.

The next line contains n%%ZSMJ36%% integers from 1%%ZSMJ37%% to n%%ZSMJ38%%, where the i%%ZSMJ39%%-th of them is the i%%ZSMJ40%%-th element of the permutation. Each integer from 1%%ZSMJ41%% to n%%ZSMJ42%% appears exactly once.
The next line contains m%%ZSMJ43%% integers from 1%%ZSMJ44%% to n%%ZSMJ45%%, the i%%ZSMJ46%%-th of them is the i%%ZSMJ47%%-th element of the array a%%ZSMJ48%%.

The next q%%ZSMJ49%% lines describe queries. The i%%ZSMJ50%%-th of these lines contains two integers li%%ZSMJ51%% and ri%%ZSMJ52%% (1≤li≤ri≤m%%ZSMJ53%%), meaning that the i%%ZSMJ54%%-th query is about the subsegment of the array from the li%%ZSMJ55%%-th to the ri%%ZSMJ56%%-th positions, inclusive.
output: Print a single string of length q%%ZSMJ57%%, consisting of 0%%ZSMJ58%% and 1%%ZSMJ59%%, the digit on the i%%ZSMJ60%%-th positions should be 1%%ZSMJ61%%, if the subsegment of array a%%ZSMJ62%% from the li%%ZSMJ63%%-th to the ri%%ZSMJ64%%-th positions, inclusive, contains a subsequence that is a cyclic shift of p%%ZSMJ65%%, and 0%%ZSMJ66%% otherwise.
note: In the first example the segment from the 1%%ZSMJ67%%-st to the 5%%ZSMJ68%%-th positions is 1,2,3,1,2%%ZSMJ69%%. There is a subsequence 1,3,2%%ZSMJ70%% that is a cyclic shift of the permutation. The subsegment from the 2%%ZSMJ71%%-nd to the 6%%ZSMJ72%%-th positions also contains a subsequence 2,1,3%%ZSMJ73%% that is equal to the permutation. The subsegment from the 3%%ZSMJ74%%-rd to the 5%%ZSMJ75%%-th positions is 3,1,2%%ZSMJ76%%, there is only one subsequence of length 3%%ZSMJ77%% (3,1,2%%ZSMJ78%%), but it is not a cyclic shift of the permutation.

In the second example the possible cyclic shifts are 1,2%%ZSMJ79%% and 2,1%%ZSMJ80%%. The subsegment from the 1%%ZSMJ81%%-st to the 2%%ZSMJ82%%-nd positions is 1,1%%ZSMJ83%%, its subsequences are not cyclic shifts of the permutation. The subsegment from the 2%%ZSMJ84%%-nd to the 3%%ZSMJ85%%-rd positions is 1,2%%ZSMJ86%%, it coincides with the permutation. The subsegment from the 3%%ZSMJ87%% to the 4%%ZSMJ88%% positions is 2,2%%ZSMJ89%%, its subsequences are not cyclic shifts of the permutation.
